paper.title: Oracle-Efficient Hybrid Online Learning with Unknown Distribution

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid online learning with unknown i.i.d. feature distribution and adaptive adversarial labels
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Full-information online prediction (supervised online learning) against a hypothesis class, not a bandit problem
unmapped: features drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution, labels in [0,1] chosen adaptively by adversary
predictions in [0,1], loss convex in first argument and L-Lipschitz in both arguments
comparator class H with bounded Rademacher complexity / VC / fat-shattering dimension
oracle-efficiency: access to mixed ERM oracle
settings.definition_quote: Nature selects an (unknown) distribution $\mu$ over $\mathcal{X}$ at the start of the game. At each time step $t$, Nature independently samples $\x_t \sim \mu$ and selects \emph{adversarially} a $y_t \in [0,1]$, but reveals only $\x_t$. A predictor then (randomly) generates $\hat{y}_t \in [0,1]$ ...

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid online learning with oblivious adversary
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Full-information online prediction, not a bandit problem
unmapped: adversary fixes label functions f_t before the game, y_t = f_t(x_t)
settings.definition_quote: the adversary fixes functions $f_1,\cdots,f_T:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow [0,1]$ before the game and sets the adversary labels $y_t=f_t(\x_t)$ for each time step $t\in [T]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid online learning with shifting distributions (K changes)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Full-information online prediction, not a bandit problem
unmapped: feature distribution is piecewise i.i.d. with at most K arbitrary change points (unknown positions)
binary-valued hypothesis class with finite VC dimension
epoch length tuned using T and K
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the total number of changes is upper bounded by $K$, while the selection of distributions and change points are completely arbitrary.

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid contextual K-arm bandits with unknown i.i.d. context distribution
unmapped: contexts i.i.d. from unknown distribution (no sampling access)
finite policy class H, access to ERM oracle
regret measured on expected loss <q_t, c_t>
settings.definition_quote: Nature selects some $\mu$ at the start of the game. At each time step $t$, Nature samples $\x_t \sim \mu$ and selects \emph{adversarially} a cost vector $c_t \in [0,1]^K$, but reveals only $\x_t$. A predictor then selects a distribution $q_t \in \mathcal{D}_K$ ... Nature reveals only $c_t[\hat{y}_t]$

algorithms.name: Epoch-based surrogate relaxation predictor with random play-out from empirical distribution
Fixed-length epoch restart of oracle-efficient predictor (shifting distributions)
Epoch-based relaxation bandit predictor (adapted from Syrgkanis et al. 2016) with hallucinated contexts from empirical distribution

symbols.q: exponent with Rad_T(H) <= O(T^q), q in [1/2,1]

conditions: loss convex in first argument and L-Lipschitz

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H} \subset [0,1]^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a class with $\mathsf{Rad}_T(\mathcal{H}) \le O(T^{q})$ for some $q \in [\frac{1}{2},1]$, and let $\ell$ be a $L$-Lipschitz loss that is convex in its first argument. Then there exists an \emph{oracle-efficient} prediction rule $\Phi$ with at most $O(L\sqrt{T}\log T)$ calls to the ERM oracle per round, such that \[\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi) \le O\left(L\sqrt{\log (LT)} \cdot T^{\frac{2-q}{3-2q}}\right).\]

results.notes: Hybrid minimax regret. Epoch schedule does not depend on T, so treated as anytime (medium confidence).

conditions: binary-valued class with finite VC dimension

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: In particular, for a binary-valued class with finite VC-dimension, we have \(\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi) \le O(L\sqrt{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{H})\log (LT)} \cdot T^{\frac{3}{4}}),\)

symbols.p_fat: exponent: alpha-fat shattering dimension of order alpha^{-p}

conditions: real-valued class with alpha-fat shattering dimension of order alpha^{-p}, p>0

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: and for a real-valued class $\mathcal{H}$ with an $\alpha$-fat shattering dimension of order $\alpha^{-p}$ for $p>0$~\citep{alon1997scale}, we have \(\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi) \le \tilde{O}(L T^{\max\{\frac{3}{4},\frac{p+1}{p+2}\}}).\)

symbols.VC_u: VC dimension of the class of pointwise suprema over subsets of H
symbols.VC_i: VC dimension of the class of pointwise infima over subsets of H

source.label: cor1
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset \{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{u}}=...$, $\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{i}}=...$ be two classes of functions and $\ell$ be the absolute loss. Then there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ satisfying $\tilde{r}_T(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O(\sqrt{\max\{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{u}}), \mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{i}})\}T})$.

conditions: X=[0,1]^d, H = all 1-Lipschitz functions under L_infinity norm

source.label: th-lipschitz
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}$ and $\ell$ be as above. Then, there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ such that $\tilde{r}_{T}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le \tilde{O}(T^{\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{d-1}{d}\}})$, and this bound is tight upto poly-logarithmic factors.

source.label: th-lipschitz
source.quote: and this bound is tight upto poly-logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Tightness claim justified only briefly via metric entropy Theta(1/eps^d); lower bound expression inferred from tightness statement.

symbols.K_chg: upper bound on number of distribution changes (paper's K)

conditions: binary-valued class with finite VC dimension

source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset \{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a binary valued class with finite VC-dimension under a convex and $L$-Lipschitz loss. Then there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ such that if the features are generated by the process with change cost $K$ and the labels are generated adversarially, then the hybrid minimax regret as (\ref{eq:hbreg}) is upper bounded by $O\left(L\sqrt{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{H})\log(LT)}K^{\frac{1}{5}}T^{\frac{4}{5}}\right).$

results.notes: Paper's K is number of changes, mapped to K_chg (S_T in learner_knows).

source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset [K]^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a finite policy set. Then there exists an oracle-efficient predictor $\Phi$ such that the hybrid bandit minimax regret defined in Section~\ref{sec:def} is upper bounded by $$\tilde{r}_T^{\mathsf{bandit}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O\left((K^{\frac{2}{3}}(\log|\mathcal{H}|)^{\frac{1}{3}}+K\sqrt{\log K})\cdot T^{\frac{4}{5}}\right).$$

results.notes: Regret on expected loss <q_t,c_t> vs best policy in hindsight. Horizon treated as anytime since epochs don't use T.

source.label: thm:obregret
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{H}\subset [0,1]^{\mathcal{X}}$ be a class of Rademacher complexity $\mathsf{Rad}_T(\mathcal{H})=O(T^q)$ for some $q\in [\frac{1}{2},1]$ and $\ell$ be the absolute loss. Then there exists an oracle-efficient prediction rule $\Phi$ with at most $O(\sqrt{T}\log T)$ calls to the ERM oracle per round, such that $\tilde{r}_{T}^{\mathsf{ob}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O(T^q)$.

source.label: thm:obregret
source.quote: In particular, for finite-VC class $\mathcal{H}$, we have $\tilde{r}_{T}^{\mathsf{ob}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le O(\sqrt{\mathsf{VC}(\mathcal{H})T})$.

source.label: thm:obregret
source.quote: For a class $\mathcal{H}$ with $\alpha$-fat shattering dimension $O(\alpha^{-p})$ for some $p>0$, we have $\tilde{r}_{T}^{\mathsf{ob}}(\mathcal{H},\Phi)\le \tilde{O}(T^{\max\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{p-1}{p}\}})$.
